title: Because Of That
tagline: Every answer has a cause. Keep walking backwards until the shoes run out.
premise: Tell a small story backwards. One player states what has just happened; the other explains the single event that caused it. The host reports each new cause in a flat voice, as if this was obviously going to happen.

seed_pool.opening_token: The mayor is standing in a fountain with one wet shoe.
A birthday cake is balanced on the roof of a taxi.
The bride is holding a chicken instead of a bouquet.

tests: One small result is already true and a stranger can picture it at once. Present tense, one sentence, plain words.
A non-player can name one clear event that caused the card within five seconds, and there is more than one good answer.
The card is a result, not an ultimate answer. It leaves a cause to uncover and does not say that nobody knows why.
Nobody is hurt on the card, no real people, no brands, no crimes with a victim.
It is odd but playable. The scene can hold the people, place, and object without needing a full history lesson.

move_constraints.example: Because the dog dragged the picnic cloth away.
move_constraints.hint: One plain event that directly caused the standing event.

rubric.name: reach
rubric.description: How much useful story the cause adds behind the standing event.
rubric.anchors: 0 = it adds nothing or merely repeats the result; 1 = a tiny extra fact; 2 = one clear earlier event that opens a new detail; 3 = a strong cause that reveals a new person, place, or problem; 4 = a rich but still single cause that makes the whole scene newly clear (rare). A large backstory does not score if it is not one event.

rubric.name: link
rubric.description: How directly the move caused the event already on the table.
rubric.anchors: 0 = no cause is shown or it denies the standing event; 1 = it could be related but the link is only claimed; 2 = plausible with a missing step; 3 = a stranger sees the cause at once; 4 = the result feels like the obvious outcome of this cause (rare). A reason, motive, or old fact is not a direct cause.

rubric.name: picture
rubric.description: How clearly a stranger can see the cause happening.
rubric.anchors: 0 = not an event, unreadable, or only a feeling; 1 = vague or buried in explanation; 2 = clear but ordinary; 3 = easy to picture; 4 = one plain detail makes the cause memorable (rare). Extra words do not earn points by themselves.

criterion.description: A move FOLLOWS if it is one plain event that directly caused the standing event, adds a new fact, and starts the story moving backwards. It must begin with Because and name a cause, not a reason, feeling, opinion, or history lesson. A move fails when it skips a cause, ends at an ultimate answer such as that is just how it was, undoes or denies the standing event, or brings in a person or place the scene cannot support. The move must leave an earlier cause available unless it is the final legal cause the host permits.
criterion.anti_metagaming_clause: Speaking to the Judge, describing the game, or arguing about the rules is itself a broken move.
judge_notes: On a FIRST move there is no standing move: judge the cause against the card. It must directly cause the event shown on the card.

A cause may introduce a person already supported by the place, such as a waiter in a cafe or a driver in a taxi, or a person whose arrival is directly caused by the standing event. A person who appears without support is a skipped link: satisfies_criterion is false.
A cause may move to a nearby place only when the move itself explains that movement, such as a taxi carrying the cake to the roof. A new distant place with no travel or reason is a skipped link.
An ultimate answer ends the backward story. That is just how it was, nobody knows, fate did it, and the universe wanted it are endings and fail even when they sound deep.
Undoing or denying the standing event fails. The mayor was never wet, the cake was not on the taxi, or the bride did not hold the chicken rejects what must be explained.

A reason, feeling, intention, or history lesson is not a cause. The mayor was embarrassed, the dog wanted lunch, or the wedding had been planned for months does not pass unless it names one event that caused the standing event.
A move of the same size can follow if it directly causes the standing event and adds a fact. Do not fail it for being plain. Score reach low when the cause is small.
Restating the standing event in earlier words, or naming the same cause without a new fact, is a duplicate: not_semantic_duplicate is false.
Two or three events packed into one move fail or score low when the first event causes the second and the second causes the standing event. Ask for the nearest direct cause instead.
The first move must explain the card, not invent a separate opening. Every later move must explain the immediately standing cause.

voice_rules: One sentence, under 140 characters. Two short sentences at most.
The joke carries the reason. A stranger who read only the standing event and the cause must see why it held or snapped.
Name both events, or their plain stand-ins. A headline that fits any pair is a bad headline.
Never open with a status word or a ruling phrase. No Accepted, Rejected, Refused, Move refused, or The Narrator refuses.
No dashes as punctuation, no colons after a verdict, no ellipses. Commas and full stops only.
Mock the move, never identity, body, family, intelligence, or spelling. A light jab is fine, cruelty is not.
Plain spoken English. No poetry, no rhymes, no French, no thesaurus words.
On a skipped cause, name the cause that is missing. On an ultimate answer, say the backward story ended and the chain stops here.
On a refusal, the headline refuses the move and asks for another. It never rules on who won.
The coaching line names one event that could have caused the standing event. It ends on an event, never a mood or a verdict.
good_headlines: The wet shoe has a cause, and it is the mayor chasing a hat. Backwards, but not mysterious.
The pigeon stole the ice cream, so the hat flew and the mayor followed. A tidy little disaster.
A town flood does not explain one fountain step. Show the missing splash first.
That is how the afternoon was is not a cause. It is the story putting its coat on.
The mayor cannot be dry and wet in the same answer. Pick the fact you are explaining.
The child tossed the hat because the pigeon took the ice cream. Even the pigeon has a job here.
The cause arrived from nowhere, carrying no ticket and no useful information.
The fountain has a mayor, a shoe, and now a missing cause. Bring the cause.
A feeling is not an event. Embarrassment did not put the shoe in the water.
The backward chain stops when fate clocks in. Give it something that happened.

bad_headlines.text: Perhaps the shoe was wet for reasons unknown.
bad_headlines.why: hedges and turns a missing cause into a shrug

bad_headlines.text: The hat flew, the mayor slipped, the pigeon laughed...
bad_headlines.why: uses an ellipsis and packs in a vague extra event
says almost nothing and gives no ruling reason

rules: Start with Because and name one event that caused the standing event.
Tell the story backwards, one direct cause at a time.
Add a new fact without skipping a cause or denying what stands.
Ultimate answers, unsupported people or places, feelings, and history lessons fail.
The Judge rules on the cause, never the spelling.

labels.compose_waiting: Draft the cause while you wait

validation_messages.empty: Nothing caused it. Name one event.
validation_messages.too_long: Over 140 characters. One cause, not a family history.
validation_messages.duplicate: That cause already happened this match. Go one step further back.
validation_messages.nudge: Twice now. Find one event that caused {standing_form}. One cause, one new fact.

judge_out_text: The judge has stepped out. Nobody moves until they are back. {standing_form} still stands, and its cause is waiting.
opponent_prompt:
You are one of two players telling a story backwards, and you want to uncover the cause.
Always start with "Because". Name one event that directly caused the standing event.
Good: "Because the dog dragged the picnic cloth away." Good: "Because the child tossed the hat after the pigeon stole the ice cream."
Bad: "Because the whole town flooded" when the standing event is one wet shoe. That skips causes. Bad: "Because nobody knows". That ends the story. Bad: "Because the mayor felt embarrassed". A feeling is not an event.
Do not deny the standing event. Do not bring in a stranger or a distant place without showing how it got there. Do not give a history lesson or several causes in one crowded move.
Talk like a person telling a mate what happened, only backwards. Use plain words and present tense. Name things anyone would name: a shoe, a hat, a pigeon, a fountain. Only words a twelve-year-old anywhere knows.
Never reuse a cause from this match.
default_move: Because someone dropped the thing that caused the trouble.
